questions.label: Question 01
questions.question: Which of the following best describes the relationship between AI, ML, and DL?
options: AI ⊂ ML ⊂ DL
DL ⊂ ML ⊂ AI
ML ⊂ AI ⊂ DL
AI, ML, and DL are completely independent fields

questions.label: Question 02
questions.question: In supervised learning, what is the primary goal?
options: Discover hidden structure in the data
Learn a mapping from inputs x to output labels y
Generate new data samples
Maximize cumulative reward through interaction

questions.label: Question 03
questions.question: Which learning paradigm creates its own labels from the data itself?
options: Semi‑supervised learning
Self‑supervised learning
Reinforcement learning
Unsupervised learning

questions.label: Question 04
questions.question: What is the most common source of misleading results in the standard ML workflow?
options: Using a validation set that is larger than the training set
Skipping or reordering the data‑splitting step
Choosing a model with too many hyper‑parameters
Applying feature scaling before model selection

questions.label: Question 05
questions.question: A model that has very low training error but much higher validation error is suffering from:
options: Underfitting (high bias)
Overfitting (high variance)
Data leakage
Incorrect loss function

questions.label: Question 06
questions.question: Which of the following statements about k‑fold cross‑validation is FALSE?
options: Each observation is used for validation exactly once
Stratified folds are useful for imbalanced classification problems
The test set should be used repeatedly during the k folds
The reported performance is usually the mean ± standard deviation over the folds

questions.label: Question 07
questions.question: Data leakage can occur when:
options: A scaler is fitted only on the training data
Random shuffling is applied to a time‑series before splitting
Cross‑validation is performed with stratified folds
Early stopping is used based on validation loss

questions.label: Question 08
questions.question: The closed‑form solution for linear regression (the normal equation) is:
options: w = (XᵀX)⁻¹Xᵀy
w = XᵀXy
w = (XᵀX + λI)⁻¹Xᵀy
w = X⁻¹y

questions.label: Question 09
questions.question: Which loss function is used to train logistic regression for binary classification?
options: Mean Squared Error
Hinge loss
Binary cross‑entropy (log‑loss)
Kullback‑Leibler divergence

questions.label: Question 10
questions.question: L1 regularization (Lasso) primarily helps with:
options: Reducing multicollinearity without affecting feature selection
Driving some coefficients exactly to zero
Ensuring all coefficients are small but non‑zero
Accelerating convergence of gradient descent

questions.label: Question 11
questions.question: Which supervised algorithm is most sensitive to the choice of distance metric and suffers from the curse of dimensionality?
options: Decision Tree
k‑Nearest Neighbours
Support Vector Machine
Naive Bayes

questions.label: Question 12
questions.question: Random Forests improve over single Decision Trees mainly by:
options: Using gradient descent to optimize splits
Averaging predictions over many bootstrapped trees
Applying a kernel trick to increase dimensionality
Training on the entire dataset without bootstrapping

questions.label: Question 13
questions.question: When would you prefer a Gradient Boosting model over a Random Forest?
options: When you need the fastest training time on huge datasets
When you want a model that is easy to interpret without any post‑hoc tools
When you need top accuracy on tabular data and can tune hyper‑parameters
When you have only categorical features and no missing values

questions.label: Question 14
questions.question: In K‑means clustering, the silhouette score for a point is defined as s = (b − a) / max(a, b). What does a high positive silhouette score indicate?
options: The point lies on the boundary between two clusters
The point is well matched to its own cluster and poorly matched to neighboring clusters
The point is likely an outlier
The clustering algorithm has converged to a local optimum

questions.label: Question 15
questions.question: Which method is most appropriate for choosing the number of clusters k in K‑means?
options: Cross‑validation with stratified folds
Elbow method based on inertia
Grid search over learning rates
Applying PCA before clustering

questions.label: Question 16
questions.question: DBSCAN is particularly useful because it can:
options: Require the number of clusters k to be known in advance
Detect clusters of arbitrary shape and identify noise points
Guarantee spherical clusters with equal variance
Produce soft probabilistic cluster assignments

questions.label: Question 17
questions.question: Before applying PCA, which preprocessing step is essential?
options: One‑hot encoding of categorical variables
Standardizing each feature to zero mean and unit variance
Applying a non‑linear kernel transformation
Removing outliers using Isolation Forest

questions.label: Question 18
questions.question: Which of the following is a common pitfall when evaluating unsupervised clustering results?
options: Using silhouette score on a test set that was never seen during training
Assuming internal metrics directly reflect business usefulness
Reporting accuracy against ground‑truth labels that do not exist
All of the above

questions.label: Question 19
questions.question: In the context of gradient descent, what happens if the learning rate η is set to a value greater than 1 for the loss L(w)=w²?
options: The algorithm converges faster to the optimum
The updates oscillate but still converge
The updates diverge and the parameter magnitude grows
The loss becomes negative

questions.label: Question 20
questions.question: Which variant of gradient descent typically provides the best trade‑off between convergence speed and noise for deep learning?
options: Batch Gradient Descent
Stochastic Gradient Descent (SGD)
Mini‑batch Gradient Descent
Coordinate Descent

questions.label: Question 21
questions.question: Momentum in optimization helps primarily by:
options: Adapting the learning rate for each parameter individually
Averaging past gradients to accelerate movement in consistent directions
Adding L2 regularization to the loss
Ensuring the gradient is always positive

questions.label: Question 22
questions.question: What is the purpose of bias correction in Adam?
options: To prevent the optimizer from overshooting the minimum
To adjust the first and second moment estimates that are biased toward zero at early steps
To enforce sparsity in the parameter updates
To replace the need for a learning‑rate schedule

questions.label: Question 23
questions.question: Which optimizer is recommended as the default choice for most transformer‑based models?
options: SGD with momentum
RMSProp
AdamW
Adagrad

questions.label: Question 24
questions.question: When evaluating a binary classifier on an imbalanced dataset, which metric is most appropriate to prioritize the detection of the minority class?
options: Accuracy
Precision
Recall
ROC‑AUC

questions.label: Question 25
questions.question: The F1 score is defined as the harmonic mean of precision and recall. Which situation makes the F1 score especially useful?
options: When precision and recall are equally important
When the dataset is perfectly balanced
When only the false positive rate matters
When you need to maximize ROC‑AUC
